title: the obligation nobody explains as a gift
hookLine: the obligation nobody explains as a gift
carry: one day that isn't yours to fill
tomorrow: why there's fire in every church

cards: Being woken up too early. Scratchy church clothes. A parent at the bottom of the stairs saying: we're going, it's an obligation.

That's how some people who grew up Catholic remember Sunday. Catholics are asked to go to Mass every Sunday, and to a kid it can sound like homework for the soul. Meanwhile the rest of the week is full.
The phone that never stops. The laundry. The emails that arrive on Saturday night.
What if the obligation was never meant as homework?

teach.h: HE RESTED ON THE SEVENTH DAY.
teach.b: Start at the very beginning of the Bible. In Genesis, God makes the world in six days, and then, in the Douay-Rheims Bible, "he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done." God rests.
Not, the tradition says, because he's tired. In the story, the day of rest is built into the world like a beam into a house.
For the Jewish people it became the Sabbath, the seventh day, kept from sunset Friday to sunset Saturday, and Jewish families keep it still. Then something happened on a different day.

teach.h: THE FIRST DAY: THE EMPTY TOMB.
teach.b: All four Gospels put the empty tomb on the first day of the week, the day after the Sabbath. Christians began gathering on that first day to break bread, and came to call it the Lord's day.
In Latin, dies Domini. In Spanish it's still domingo, in Italian domenica.

teach.h: JUSTIN: ON THE DAY CALLED SUNDAY.
teach.b: An early Christian named Justin Martyr described it for outsiders: on the day called Sunday, everyone gathers, the memoirs of the apostles or the writings of the prophets are read, bread and wine are brought and blessed, and there's a collection for widows and orphans.
That's recognizably the Mass. So why call it an obligation?

Catholics say it's the way the Church makes sure the gift actually gets opened. Left alone, a week fills every hour. The obligation holds one day open: for worship, for family, for rest, for a long meal.

Sunday Mass can also be kept on Saturday evening, at what's called the vigil. And it isn't a trap: the Church itself says a serious reason, like being sick or caring for a baby, excuses you. The idea underneath is simple.
One day a week isn't yours to fill.

how: Catholics are asked to attend Mass every Sunday (or on Saturday evening) and on certain holy days, and to keep the day for worship, family and rest as far as they can.

games.q: what's inside the day — tap the pairs.

s: Christians gathered on Sunday because it was the Sabbath
the Sabbath is the seventh day. Christians gathered on the first day, the day of the resurrection.
the Spanish word domingo comes from "the Lord's day"
Catholics can keep Sunday Mass on Saturday evening
the vigil Mass counts for Sunday.

games.q: you're an early Christian, and outsiders want to know what you do on the day called Sunday. what does Justin Martyr tell them?
o: we gather, read the apostles, bless bread and wine, and collect for the poor.
games.why: Justin's description is recognizably the Mass, down to the collection.

practice: Here's the practice, and for this sit you have nothing to do. Nothing to fill. Put the phone face down, or out of reach.
Let your hands rest open. Every time your mind reaches for a task, notice it, and set it down for later. If you pray, you can offer the time to God.
If not, just let it be empty.

wordCard.voice: Sunday. The Lord's day, the day of the empty tomb, the day the Church keeps open for worship and rest. Fourteenth word.

orig.note: Greek: the Lord's day, from Revelation 1:10. Latin made it dies Domini.

carryVoice: Your line: one day that isn't yours to fill. That's what the obligation was protecting all along. Two weeks, done.
